stories.headline: Tidal to ban AI-generated music from December 9 and remove millions of tracks
stories.summary: Tidal will stop allowing fully AI-generated music on December 9 and will delete roughly 29 million such songs. It expects to reject about 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day, and it will still accept AI-assisted work.
stories.why: Platforms are tightening content rules on AI-made material, which affects anyone building music, content, or catalog-moderation tools.

sources.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming

stories.headline: Anthropic study finds many enterprise AI rollouts stall for organizational reasons
stories.summary: Anthropic reviewed nearly 300 AI deployments at 58 US companies. About one in five delivered no business value, mainly because of heavy review workloads, internal bottlenecks, and employee resistance, which the researchers link to outdated company structures.
stories.why: Engineering leaders planning AI adoption may find the blockers are process and org design rather than tooling skills.

sources.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools

stories.headline: Amazon reports attackers' AI agents found and exploited a zero-day with little human input
stories.summary: Amazon says hackers used AI agents, built on a framework called Cairn AI, to find and exploit a previously unknown vulnerability with minimal human guidance. The company notes the same tooling can help defenders.
stories.why: Autonomous exploit discovery shortens the window teams have to patch, so security practices need to keep pace.

sources.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

stories.headline: Google DeepMind uses AI agents to run experiments for Gemini development
stories.summary: DeepMind has AI agents run experiments for upcoming Gemini models, with some compute under their control. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement. The agents' internal reasoning is left untrained on purpose so humans can review it.
stories.why: It shows agents moving into real research workflows, and the oversight approach offers a model for reviewing autonomous tooling.

sources.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant

stories.headline: Anthropic's MCP SDK passes 700 million monthly downloads and adds agent features
stories.summary: Anthropic reports more than 700 million monthly downloads of the MCP SDK, two years after launch. New features include background tasks, follow-up questions to users, and file uploads, intended to let Claude work more independently.
stories.why: MCP's growing adoption and new async and agent capabilities affect how developers design tool integrations.

sources.title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents

stories.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, outperforming rivals on LiveBench
stories.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Neon beats Astra and Fable on the LiveBench benchmark. It also cuts the runtime of one TypeScript-to-Rust benchmark by 48.6 percent.
stories.why: A new frontier model release changes which models teams should evaluate for coding and production workloads.

sources.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab

stories.headline: Java4Shell: Patch fix for HotSpot Base64 decoder memory corruption flaw (CVE-2026-114938)
stories.summary: Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes on November 17 for CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption bug in the HotSpot JVM's Base64 decoder, reported by researcher Calif. JetBrains is urging users to update its IDEs and related tools.
stories.why: Any team running Java workloads or developer tools built on the JVM should check its JDK versions and apply the fixes.

sources.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability: Update Your JetBrains IDEs, ReSharper, .NET Tools, Toolbox App, and Gateway Now

stories.headline: Reported active intrusion campaign targets Check Point security management servers
stories.summary: A Hacker News discussion highlights an active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers. The item gives few details beyond the report itself.
stories.why: Security management servers control firewalls across networks, so teams using Check Point should verify their exposure and patch status.

sources.title: Active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers

stories.headline: AWS Lambda doubles maximum timeout to 30 minutes in all commercial regions
stories.summary: AWS raised the maximum timeout for on-demand Lambda event functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in and no price change. The 15-minute limit had been in place since 2018.
stories.why: Longer timeouts let teams move more long-running work into Lambda, but AWS notes effects on concurrency and queue visibility settings.

sources.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
AWS Weekly Roundup: Local Zone in Bogotá, 30-minute Lambda timeout, and more (November 24, 2026)

stories.headline: Rust 1.100 stabilises the never type after a decade of work
stories.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released November 12, stabilises the never type (!) and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core allocator API, adds DropGuard, and adds an opt-in dependency cooldown setting for Cargo.
stories.why: The dependency cooldown option gives teams a new lever against fast-moving or compromised crate versions in their build pipelines.

sources.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts

stories.headline: OpenAI details Pando, a Git backend built for concurrent coding agents
stories.summary: OpenAI described Pando, a new backend that scales Git for many concurrent coding-agent workloads while keeping standard Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by updating branches independently and reusing stored packfiles.
stories.why: As agents push code in parallel, Git server bottlenecks become a real constraint for platform and developer-tooling teams.

sources.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando

stories.headline: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after near-24-hour Outlook outage
stories.summary: Microsoft has declared an unusual internal 'Code Red' after an Exchange Online and Outlook outage that took down email for millions of customers for nearly a day. A bug on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers triggered it.
stories.why: A single networking defect caused a day-long, widespread failure, a reminder for engineering leaders to review gateway change safety and blast-radius controls.

sources.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage

stories.headline: VMware ships third critical patch bundle in a week, including another vCenter flaw
stories.summary: VMware has released its third bundle of critical patches in a week, fixing four more critical vulnerabilities. One of them is another unauthorized access flaw in vCenter.
stories.why: Repeated critical vCenter access flaws in quick succession mean teams running VMware infrastructure should prioritise these patches before the holiday period.

sources.title: This could mess with Thanksgiving, says VMware as it drops third critical patch bundle in a week

stories.headline: US Treasury's FinCEN investigates a cybersecurity incident
stories.summary: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, part of the Treasury Department, disclosed that it is investigating a cybersecurity incident. It said unauthorized access hit a limited subset of its systems, and it has not released further details.
stories.why: Confirmed unauthorized access at a federal agency is a reminder that security monitoring and access review matter for internal systems too.

sources.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’

stories.headline: Australia nears passage of Digital Duty of Care Bill with large potential fines
stories.summary: Australian lawmakers are close to passing the Digital Duty of Care Bill, an amendment to the Online Safety Act 2021. It could bring large fines for technology platforms.
stories.why: The bill could add legal duties and steep penalties for platforms operating in Australia, which will affect product, trust and safety, and compliance work.

sources.title: Australia to pass safety bill that could result in massive fines for tech platforms

stories.headline: US jury finds Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets, acquits it of racketeering
stories.summary: A federal jury in New York found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, including source code and proprietary technology from several companies. It acquitted the company of racketeering charges.
stories.why: The verdict concerns the theft of source code and proprietary technology, which highlights legal risk around code provenance and trade secret protection.

sources.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
Jury finds Huawei stole US tech, laundered money, and broke sanctions
Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, US jury rules

stories.headline: Claude-BugHunter, a Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting, trends on GitHub
stories.summary: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work gained about 1,800 GitHub stars in a day. It includes 84 skills and 15 slash commands. Its popularity is a sign of interest, not evidence of how well it works.
stories.why: Shows strong developer interest in packaging security workflows as agent skills, which raises questions about dual use and review.

sources.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 84 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerabilit

stories.headline: CLI-Anything pitches agent-native command lines for all software
stories.summary: The CLI-Anything project, which describes making all software agent-native, gained about 1,000 GitHub stars today. It also points to a CLI-Hub. The project's claims are still unproven.
stories.why: If agents can drive existing tools through standard command lines, integration work for teams could shift toward wrapping tools rather than building new APIs.

sources.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

stories.headline: Superpowers, an agentic skills framework, keeps climbing GitHub Trending
stories.summary: The obra/superpowers project, billed as an agentic skills framework and software development methodology, added about 1,000 stars today and has over 326,000 in total. Its wide reach is visible, but its real-world results are not shown in these items.
stories.why: Many engineering teams are experimenting with methods for coding agents, so this framework is a useful reference for how others structure agent workflows.

sources.title: obra/superpowers: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

stories.headline: Cursor publishes a plugin specification and official plugins
stories.summary: The cursor/plugins repository now holds a plugin specification and official plugins for Cursor, and gained about 360 stars today. The project is early and its adoption is still uncertain.
stories.why: A public plugin spec could make Cursor extensions more portable and give teams a clearer way to standardise their editor tooling.

sources.title: cursor/plugins: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins

stories.headline: Minimind offers a 64M-parameter LLM trained from scratch in about two hours
stories.summary: The minimind project, which trains a 64M-parameter language model from scratch in roughly two hours, gained about 730 stars today. The claim is a small-scale demonstration, not a full-size model result.
stories.why: It lowers the cost of learning how LLMs are built and gives engineers a hands-on way to understand training pipelines.

sources.title: jingyaogong/minimind: 🧠 两小时从 0 训出你的 64M 大模型。Train your own 64M LLM from scratch in 2 hours.

stories.headline: JetBrains CEO gives manual code review two years before it fades
stories.summary: JetBrains' chief executive predicts that manual code review may be largely replaced within about two years. LeadDev covers the claim.
stories.why: If review becomes automated, teams will need new standards for approval, accountability, and the reviewer's role.

sources.title: The end of manual code review?

stories.headline: Less experienced developers trust AI more, eroding code ownership
stories.summary: LeadDev reports that junior developers tend to trust AI output more than senior engineers do, and that this is weakening ownership of code.
stories.why: Leaders may need to rethink review standards and who is accountable for AI-assisted code.

sources.title: Code ownership is eroding

stories.headline: Engineer reports 100+ production PRs in one week and metrics caveats
stories.summary: Will Larson says he shipped more than 100 pull requests to production in a single week, reaching 115 in the week of November 9. He reports a seven-day peak of 170 merged PRs.
stories.why: A concrete throughput example shows how volume numbers can be inflated or misread when used as productivity measures.

sources.title: Shipping 100+ PRs to production in a week

stories.headline: Cannabis users develop psychosis about 2.5 years earlier, with the gap widening with age
stories.summary: An analysis of 149 studies found cannabis users developed psychosis on average 2.5 years earlier than non-users. Among adults aged 30 and older, the gap grew to more than six years, and researchers warn the risks may accumulate over time.
stories.why: It suggests cumulative mental health risks that workplace wellbeing and substance policies may need to account for.

sources.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

stories.headline: AI models that predict brain activity may use processes the brain does not
stories.summary: Researchers found that AI models which closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes that the brain does not use. The finding challenges how scientists interpret such models as analogues of human thinking.
stories.why: Matching neural data does not mean a model reasons like a person, which matters when teams interpret AI behaviour.

sources.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover

stories.headline: Cynical hostility and difficulty saying no predict depression 23 years later
stories.summary: Tracking 1,017 Swedish twin pairs over 23 years, researchers found that cynical hostility and lack of assertiveness each predicted more depression later in life. The link held even between identical twins.
stories.why: It adds long-term evidence that interpersonal traits are tied to mental health, relevant to team climate and wellbeing.

sources.title: Cynical hostility and lack of assertiveness both predict depression decades later

stories.headline: Problematic smartphone use predicts a rebound in attention issues in late adolescence
stories.summary: A study tracking thousands of teenagers found attention symptoms tend to decline in early adolescence before rising again as adulthood approaches. Struggling to control smartphone use predicted worse behavioural problems over time.
stories.why: It adds evidence on how device habits relate to later behaviour, relevant to products and policies aimed at young users.

sources.title: Problematic smartphone use predicts a rebound in attention issues during late adolescence

stories.headline: Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO after resignation over reported affairs
stories.summary: Huang returned as Nvidia's chief executive after resigning amid reported affairs, one allegedly with a woman suspected of spying for Beijing. Nvidia shares initially rallied, then fell as investors weighed legal and regulatory risk, and lawmakers are scrutinising the reinstatement.
stories.why: Leadership turmoil at the largest AI chip supplier could affect GPU supply, pricing and regulatory exposure across the AI tooling market.

sources.title: Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan
Jensen Huang to face DC grilling the same day Nvidia releases new products at GTC

stories.headline: Dell beats earnings on AI server demand and authorises $25 billion buyback
stories.summary: Dell reported third-quarter earnings above expectations, with sales more than doubling year on year, driven by demand for AI servers. The company also authorised a $25 billion share buyback.
stories.why: Strong AI server demand signals continued infrastructure spending that shapes hardware availability and cloud costs for engineering teams.

sources.title: Dell earnings beat on AI strength, company authorizes $25 billion buyback

stories.headline: Lenders grow pickier on Big Tech bonds as AI build-out spending rises
stories.summary: Reporting says Big Tech may find it harder to raise funds from debt markets, which are critical to the AI infrastructure build-out, as lenders become more selective over corporate bonds.
stories.why: If financing tightens, the pace of data centre and AI capacity expansion could slow, affecting compute availability and vendor roadmaps.

sources.title: AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze

stories.headline: Hotter inflation data points to a likely Fed rate hike in December
stories.summary: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose to 3.8% in October, and core PCE came in at 3.3% year on year, slightly above forecasts. Analysts expect the central bank to raise interest rates next month.
stories.why: Higher borrowing costs raise the price of financing cloud spend, startups and large engineering projects.

sources.title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge accelerated to 3.8% in October, likely sealing rate hike
Core PCE Price Index rises 3.3% Y/Y, slightly hotter than expected
